title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors and officers of the Company including the Managing Director; all direct reports to the Managing Director ('Senior Executives'); their associates (as defined in the Corporations Act) including close family members and trusts and entities controlled by them; and other persons identified by the Company from time to time. This tier alone is subject to blackout periods, the no short-term/speculative trading rule, notification and clearance, and the hedging/derivatives ban, on top of the general insider trading prohibition.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair, a Restricted Person; distinguished only for clearance, notifying and obtaining consent from the Board.

tiers.name: Other Directors (including Managing Director)
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, including the Managing Director; distinguished only for clearance (Chair of the Board).

tiers.name: Senior Executives and other persons identified by the Company from time to time
tiers.description: Direct reports to the Managing Director and other persons the Company identifies as Restricted Persons; distinguished only for clearance (Chair of the Board).

tiers.name: Directors and employees
tiers.description: All Directors and employees of the Company and their associates, to the extent not Restricted Persons; subject only to the general insider trading prohibition and confidentiality duty, with no blackout, clearance, short-term or hedging restrictions under this policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities

windows.start_anchor: close of trading at the end of each quarter (31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December)
windows.end_anchor: 10.00am on the next trading day following the announcement to the ASX of the quarterly results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may specify 'any other period' as a blackout period from time to time (rule 6.3); the policy does not state whether such a period is confidential.

rules.detail: Dealing in derivatives, including put and call options, is expressly named and banned without prior written approval from the person in rule 7. The provision extends to Securities that are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued under an equity remuneration scheme, so both legs of an OTC collar need clearance regardless of vesting state.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not, without prior written approval by the relevant person specified in rule 7, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference

rules.detail: Named hedging ban, requiring prior written approval, expressly extended to unvested, holding-locked and equity-scheme Securities as well as vested unrestricted holdings.
rules.evidence: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with Company Securities including Securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward sale) is not named, but the 6.9 catch-all for arrangements that 'vary economic risk' or are 'intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price' is broad enough to sweep it in, requiring the same prior written approval as hedging.
rules.evidence: enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities ... and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere; the closest provision (6.4) addresses short-term/speculative trading generally, not the borrow-and-sell mechanics of short selling.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Contracts for difference are expressly named as an example caught by the hedging/derivatives approval requirement.
rules.evidence: including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not named and there is no defined 'Dealing' provision sweeping in the grant of security; the policy is entirely silent on financing arrangements over Company Securities.
Granting a charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not mentioned; there is no encumbrance provision or definition of 'dealing' extending to it.

No provision addresses secured financing, margin loans or any borrowing secured against Company Securities. The 6.9 catch-all is confined to arrangements that vary or limit economic risk (hedging-type instruments), not financing structures as such.
General discouragement of short-term or speculative trading, expressed as 'should not' rather than an absolute 'must not', with no defined holding period, LIFO basis or numeric threshold.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company's Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as reasonably practicable; for Directors, no later than three business days after the date of the change (for ASX reporting)
clearance.evidence: If granted, trading consent is only valid for a period of 5 trading days after notification of approval. Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as reasonably practicable; no later than three business days after the date of the change (for ASX reporting)
clearance.evidence: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn or refused by the Company in its discretion without giving any reasons. A decision to refuse approval is final and binding on the person seeking the approval.

clearance.tier: Senior Executives and other persons identified by the Company from time to time
clearance.evidence: If approval to trade Company Securities is refused, the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.

short_term.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company's Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain.

exceptions.approver: Person specified in rule 7 for the Restricted Person's tier
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances include severe financial hardship, compulsion by a court order or any other circumstances that are deemed exceptional by the person described in rule 7.

exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances include severe financial hardship, compulsion by a court order or any other circumstances that are deemed exceptional by the person described in rule 7.

exceptions.evidence: or any other circumstances that are deemed exceptional by the person described in rule 7.
the additional restrictions in this policy do not prohibit Restricted Persons from acquiring Securities under a Company dividend reinvestment plan or an employee share plan
The additional restrictions in this policy do not affect a Restricted Person's participation in any Company employee share or option plans or the exercise of options/rights under those plans.

exemption_authority: The Board (for the Chair) or the Chair of the Board (for other Directors and Senior Executives) may grant a waiver from the blackout or short-term trading rules in exceptional circumstances (rule 6.5), and may give, withhold, condition or withdraw approval to trade under rule 6.6 in its discretion without giving reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with Company Securities including Securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's put and call legs need prior written approval from the rule 7 approver even if written over unvested or holding-locked equity award shares, not only fully vested unrestricted stock.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no provision addressing margin lending, encumbrance, custodial transfer or any other secured financing arrangement over Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not expressly prohibited or made subject to clearance or disclosure, but the bank should obtain the Company's written confirmation, since the broad 'vary economic risk' language in 6.9 could arguably be read by the Company to capture the financing structure as a whole.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If granted, trading consent is only valid for a period of 5 trading days after notification of approval. Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be priced and executed within 5 trading days of clearance, and clearance evaporates automatically if inside information arises beforehand, so timing risk sits with the executive and the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn or refused by the Company in its discretion without giving any reasons... the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company can refuse or withdraw clearance for the collar without explanation, and the executive cannot disclose a refusal to the bank, which is a practical execution risk for the transaction timeline.

bespoke_clauses.clause: their associates (as defined in the Corporations Act) including, close family members and trusts and entities controlled by them
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled entity does not escape the clearance and hedging restrictions that apply to the Restricted Person.

summary: A funded collar is conditionally possible for a Nickel Industries director or Senior Executive, but only with prior written approval: clause 6.9 expressly names put and call options and CFDs and bans dealing in derivatives or hedging without approval from the Chair (or the Board, for the Chair), and this ban explicitly extends even to unvested or holding-locked shares. Approved trades must fall outside the roughly one-month quarterly blackout window, be executed within 5 trading days of clearance, and lapse automatically if inside information arises. The policy is entirely silent on margin lending, encumbrance and secured financing, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is not expressly prohibited or regulated, but the bank should seek the Company's written comfort given the breadth of the 'vary economic risk' language. Refusal of approval is confidential and given in the Company's unfettered discretion, and short-term or speculative trading is discouraged, favouring a longer collar tenor.
